title: The Last Page, Then the Shuffle
skyStory: One year ago the moon was brand new, two percent lit in Sagittarius, pretending to be asleep while this page woke up. Tonight it is eighty percent bright in Pisces and wide awake, misty-eyed. Mars brought the same streamers. Saturn brought the same clipboard, every box ticked. The deck sits on the table, ready to be gathered, shuffled, and dealt again.

reading: A year ago tomorrow, the very first reading told you to plant one seed and walk away whistling. Look at the garden now. The Tiger learned, slowly and with a great deal of grumbling, to say thank you and mean it. That is no small summit.

Tonight, before bed, switch the onyx to your right wrist one last time this year and send all of it up the mountain: the jokes, the missions, the mittens, the rowboat. Then switch it back and let something return. The [[Six of Pentacles]] says the giving and receiving are even now. The cards will be reshuffled tomorrow, and the Fire will be ready.
joel.mission: Find the tiny folded sentence from last November, or write a new one, and read it aloud to the cabin.
joel.omen: A chimney puffing smoke in a straight line, just like the first day. The circle is closed and the fire still burns.

reading: A year ago you turned the ruby outward like a tiny lighthouse, and the sky has been following that beam ever since. Story after story, crossing after crossing, your hands dancing the whole way. The Mountain did not move. It did not need to. Everything came to it.

Tonight the moon is nearly full in Pisces, soft and generous. Set the ruby beside the onyx under a window and let them glow side by side for one breath. Then say thank you to the year in your own words. [[The World]] waits to close the circle. Tomorrow the deck shuffles, a new moon of readings begins, and the Light Returning will be dealt a fresh, bright hand.
nancy.mission: Tell the story of your favourite day this year, with your hands, to someone who has not heard it.
nancy.omen: A gull standing on one leg somewhere it should not be, just like the first day. Bold choices remain in season.
nancy.stoneWhy: the Fire's stone, a year strong

together.text: On the first day you each sent one word for how the month should feel. Tonight, send one word for how the whole year felt. Compare at bedtime. Then the cards get gathered, shuffled and dealt again, and the next adventure begins tomorrow.
